decision.check: All visible faces, walls, rims and edges.
decision.defect_when: A localized corrosion pattern is visibly present on intact metal: mottled brown, orange, red, or rust-like discoloration accompanied by corrosion texture such as pitting, roughness, flaking, or an irregular oxidized patch. A single thin scratch, stain, dark line, or small isolated discoloration without corrosion texture is not corrosion.
decision.clear_when: No localized oxidized/corroded pattern with supporting corrosion texture is visible.
decision.review_when: Color or texture is too obscured to distinguish genuine oxidation/corrosion from a scratch, stain, finish variation, shadow, or normal surface texture.
ignore: Thin scratches or linear surface marks without oxidation texture.
Small isolated discoloration without mottled corrosion texture.
decision.boundary: Corrosion requires both a corrosion-like appearance and supporting surface texture; do not classify a generic brown/dark mark as corrosion. Missing material or a broken silhouette is edge_chip.
decision.localization: Tight box around each distinct corrosion patch.

decision.check: Sweep the complete visible surface and follow any candidate line end-to-end.
decision.defect_when: One thin, defined, continuous bright/bare-metal groove runs across a substantial distance of the surface.
decision.clear_when: Only normal grain, short polishing streaks, or no continuous groove is visible.
decision.review_when: Glare, blur or occlusion prevents deciding whether a candidate line is continuous and defined.
decision.boundary: A localized 3D depression is dent; a dark connected patch is dark_mark.
decision.localization: Tight box around each distinct line mark.

decision.check: Sweep faces, rims, edges, collars and flanges for contour changes.
decision.defect_when: Metal is pushed/deformed inward while material remains present, with a localized broken contour or depression.
decision.clear_when: The contour is intact and no localized 3D deformation is visible.
decision.review_when: There is not enough depth/contour evidence to distinguish deformation from a line or reflection.
ignore: Specular highlights on an intact contour.
decision.boundary: Missing material is edge_chip; a flat continuous groove is line_mark.
decision.localization: Tight box around each distinct dent/deformation.

decision.check: Trace the entire outer silhouette, rim and every flange/edge.
decision.defect_when: A notch, sheared break or chipped section shows material missing from an otherwise continuous silhouette.
decision.clear_when: The full visible silhouette is intact.
decision.review_when: The edge is cropped, blurred or obscured where a break may exist.
ignore: Reddish staining on an intact edge.
Pushed-in material with no missing section.
decision.boundary: Reddish oxidation on intact metal is corrosion; deformation without missing material is dent.
decision.localization: Tight box around each missing-material notch.

decision.check: Sweep the whole visible surface, every outer edge/rim and every hole/feature border.
decision.defect_when: A clearly visible, distinct, localized dark surface blemish is present on the metal and has a clear local footprint that is reportable as a marking. It may be small or large and may be dark gray, brown-black, purple-gray, or near-black; near-black color or extreme contrast is not required. A bounded dark patch or smear with a visible local boundary, including a dark area adjacent to or surrounding a hole but outside the bore/shadow, is reportable when it is visually distinct from the normal finish. When the blemish is connected, patch-like, irregular, or elongated, classify it as dark_mark.
decision.clear_when: No clearly visible, distinct, reportable dark surface marking is present.
decision.review_when: A candidate dark region is visible but its local boundary or surface character cannot be reliably separated from hole shadow, normal finish/passivation, glare, shadow, lighting gradient, or image noise.
ignore: Diffuse lighting gradients without a bounded blemish.
Tiny incidental specks, isolated noise, or insignificant surface variation that would not reasonably be reported as a defect.
decision.enumeration: Report every distinct reportable dark_mark with its own tight box.
decision.localization: Tight box around the actual dark marking, not the surrounding metal.
decision.boundary: Dark_mark is based on a distinct reportable surface blemish, not near-black color or a minimum size. A bounded connected/patch-like/irregular/elongated dark area can be dark_mark even at moderate contrast. Exclude the hole bore and its shadow; classify a compact isolated spot as dark_spot.

decision.check: Sweep the entire visible metal surface systematically, including the area around markings, holes, edges and transitions.
decision.defect_when: A clearly visible, distinct localized dark surface blemish is present and is significant enough to be a reportable defect. This includes a small or medium bounded darker patch/discoloration with a clear local footprint, even when it is gray, brownish, muted, or only moderately darker than the surrounding metal. The blemish may be a single compact spot, a narrow irregular spot, or a small localized cluster of multiple dark spots. It does not need to be circular or have a minimum width. A visible cluster of several meaningful dark spots in one local area is still reportable dark_spot evidence; do not dismiss it merely because each individual spot is small. Do not require near-black color or extreme contrast when the local boundary and darker surface feature are clearly visible.
decision.clear_when: The inspected surface has no clearly visible, distinct, reportable localized dark blemish or localized cluster of reportable dark spots.
decision.review_when: A localized dark feature is visible but resolution, glare, shadow or finish variation prevents deciding whether it is a real reportable surface blemish.
ignore: Diffuse lighting gradient without a bounded footprint.
Tiny incidental specks, isolated image noise, or insignificant dark variation that would not reasonably be reported as a defect.
decision.boundary: Dark_spot is based on a localized reportable blemish or localized cluster, not a minimum pixel size. A genuinely reportable spot may be small. Do not convert a small localized cluster into dark_mark merely because it contains several spots. Use dark_mark for a connected patch-like or clearly mark-like feature; if the feature is only incidental or insignificant, report neither.
decision.enumeration: Report each distinct reportable dark_spot separately when they are clearly separable. When several meaningful dark spots form one localized cluster and individual boxes would be impractical, report the cluster with one tight area box. Do not report incidental or insignificant specks merely because they are visible.
decision.localization: Use a tight box around the actual dark spot or the localized cluster of reportable dark spots, not the surrounding metal.

decision.check: Sweep the whole visible surface, edges/rims and feature borders.
decision.defect_when: A localized pale/dull low-luster patch contrasts with surrounding metal while underlying grain remains visible.
decision.clear_when: No localized dull/pale patch is present.
decision.review_when: Brightness and luster are too obscured to distinguish a dull patch from glare.
ignore: Specular highlight that is brighter and washes out grain.
decision.localization: Tight box around each localized dull/pale patch.
